thread.title: Trump said the US won't attack Iran before November. Oil prices eased and the Sensex rose 879 points.
thread.dek: How a US decision about Iran affected India's oil bill, prices and share market within a day. Bargain buying and good IT results also helped the market.

Fear of war eases, oil prices dip
nodes.note: Analysts linked the 9 Oct rally to cheaper oil

nodes.label: India's oil import bill and the rupee
nodes.note: India buys over 85% of its oil from abroad

thread.classLine: How can a US election affect an Indian home loan? Answer: through oil prices, then inflation, then the RBI's interest rate.

stories.headline: RBI raises its key interest rate to 5.50% to fight rising prices
stories.summary: On 7 October, the RBI raised the repo rate by 0.25 percentage point to 5.50%. This is its first increase since February 2023. All six members of its Monetary Policy Committee voted for it. The RBI said it may raise rates again if needed and will not cut them soon. It expects prices to rise 5.2% this year and the economy to grow 7.1%.

chain.label: Prices rising, oil above $100
RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%
Loan and deposit rates go up
People borrow and spend a little less, so prices rise more slowly

stories.eureka: In 2025 the RBI cut rates four times. Within a year it has started raising them again. A big reason is a war thousands of kilometres away that pushed oil prices up.
stories.context: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to banks. When it goes up, banks usually raise their loan and deposit rates. Through 2025 the RBI cut this rate from 6.50% to 5.25% to support growth. Prices have now been rising for ten months in a row, with oil above $100 a barrel adding to the pressure.

stories.headline: The US raised its interest rate, and foreign money flowed out of India
stories.summary: On 16 September, the US central bank (the Federal Reserve) raised its interest rate to 3.75–4.00%, its first increase since 2023. When US rates rise, investors can earn more in America, so some pull money out of countries like India. In September, foreign investors sold ₹35,861 crore more Indian shares than they bought. The rupee stayed near 96 to the dollar.

chain.label: US raises its interest rate
US investments pay more, dollar gets stronger
Foreign investors sell Indian shares
Rupee falls; RBI sells dollars to steady it

stories.eureka: A vote in Washington can make money tighter in India without the RBI doing anything. The US does not set India's rates, but it sets the return that foreign investors compare India against.
stories.concept: Why US interest rates move the rupee
stories.context: The US Federal Reserve sets interest rates for the world's biggest economy. Its decisions move the dollar and the flow of investment around the world, so they affect India even though India's own rates are set by the RBI.

stories.headline: Trump says no US attack on Iran before November, and oil prices ease
stories.summary: On 8 October, US President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the US elections on 3 November. The US–Iran war began in February. Attacks on oil tankers have made the Strait of Hormuz, a key sea route for oil, risky to use. In July India stopped loading some oil from Iraq and is buying more Russian oil, about 2.45 million barrels a day.

chain.label: Risk of a US strike on Iran falls
Oil prices ease
India's oil import bill
Less pressure on the rupee, prices and interest rates

stories.eureka: India's oil bill now depends partly on the date of a US election. One narrow sea route carries a big share of India's inflation risk.
stories.concept: Supply shock: when costs push prices up
stories.context: India buys more than 85% of its oil from abroad. Before the war, about half of it came from the Middle East, much of it through the Strait of Hormuz. Any threat to that route raises the price India pays for oil.

stories.headline: Why the CJP protests did not shake the stock market
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by Abhijeet Dipke, began in anger over leaks in competitive exams and spread to Delhi, demanding the Education Minister's resignation. Activist Sonam Wangchuk fasted for 26 days, and a march to Parliament on 20 July turned violent. Analysts said the protests did not move share prices. In July, foreign investors bought ₹15,157 crore more Indian shares than they sold, even as the protests grew.

chain.label: Street protests in Delhi
Investors ask: will policy change?
Only policy, tax or spending changes matter
So far, little effect on shares

stories.eureka: Markets react to changes in policy, not to noise on the street. In the very month the protests peaked, foreign investors were buying Indian shares.
stories.concept: Political risk and how investors judge it
stories.statusNote: These reports are from July. I could not find October updates on the protest.
stories.context: Investors worry about protests when they might change government policy, taxes or spending. Analysts quoted at the time said these protests had not done that, so they mattered less to markets than oil prices, US interest rates and tariffs.

stories.headline: GST collection crossed ₹2 lakh crore, helped by tax on imports
stories.summary: The government collected ₹2.04 lakh crore in GST in September, 14.7% more than a year ago. GST on imported goods rose 25.9%, while GST on goods and services sold within India rose 10.1%. From April to September, GST on imports is up 27.1% and GST within India is up 6.1%. These are early figures and may change. The release does not explain the gap.

chain.label: A dollar costs about 8% more rupees than a year ago
GST on imports is charged on rupee value
GST on imports rises
Part of the rise may be the weak rupee, not more buying

stories.eureka: Oil is not taxed under GST yet, so this is not about oil. One reason for the jump: a weaker rupee raises the rupee value of imports, and GST is charged on that value. A weak currency can make tax collection look stronger than the economy really is.
stories.concept: Why a weak rupee can raise tax collection
stories.context: GST is India's main tax on goods and services. On imports it is charged as IGST, on the value of the goods in rupees. So when the rupee weakens, the same imported item carries more tax in rupees.

stories.headline: New 10% US tax on Indian goods covers more than half of India's exports to America
stories.summary: On 24 July, the US announced a 10% import tax (tariff) on Indian goods, on top of normal duties. The US says it targets goods made with forced labour, and it applies to 60 countries. About 45% of India's exports to the US are exempt, such as generic medicines, smartphones, steel, aluminium and car parts. So 55% are covered. Clothes and textiles are hit hardest. India says it still wants a trade deal with the US.

chain.label: US adds a 10% tariff
Indian goods cost more in the US
Textile and clothing exports
Jobs in small textile units at risk

stories.eureka: The US says the tariff is about working conditions, not trade. This shows how rules on labour and human rights are becoming new ways to restrict trade.
stories.context: The US is one of India's biggest export markets. A tariff makes Indian goods costlier for American buyers, so they may buy from other countries instead.

stories.headline: TCS profit rises 15%, and AI work is now a tenth of its business
stories.summary: TCS, India's largest IT company, made a profit of ₹13,934 crore in July–September, 14.9% more than a year earlier. Its revenue rose 11.2% to ₹73,188 crore. AI-related work now brings in $3.1 billion a year, over 10% of its revenue. It signed new deals worth $9.6 billion and added 4,258 staff. IT shares led the market on 9 October, up 3%.

chain.label: Rupee near 96 to the dollar
Each dollar earned is worth more rupees
IT profits and service exports
Service exports help pay for India's imports

stories.eureka: The same weak rupee that hurts oil importers helps IT companies. One exchange rate creates winners and losers at the same time. That is why the RBI tries to stop sharp swings rather than fix the rupee at one level.
stories.context: IT companies earn mostly in dollars but pay most of their costs in rupees. When the rupee weakens, each dollar they earn is worth more rupees.

stories.headline: Economy grew 7.8%, which gave the RBI room to raise rates
stories.summary: India's economy grew 7.8% in April–June, faster than the RBI expected. The RBI then raised its growth forecast for the year to 7.1% and raised interest rates.

chain.label: Growth beats estimates
Economy running strong
Less risk that higher rates cause a slowdown
RBI raises rates with confidence

stories.eureka: Good news on growth can lead to higher interest rates. Students often think rates go up only in bad times, but a strong economy is often what makes a rate rise possible.
stories.context: GDP growth measures how fast the economy's total output is rising. Higher interest rates usually slow growth a little, so a central bank finds it easier to raise rates when growth is strong.

concept.explain: A country cannot have all three at once: a fixed exchange rate, money flowing freely in and out, and its own interest-rate policy. It has to give up one.
concept.today: India keeps money flows open: foreign investors sold ₹35,861 crore of shares in September without any restriction. The RBI also sets its own interest rate, and raised it on 7 Oct. So the exchange rate has to give: the rupee has slipped to near 96. The RBI sold dollars to slow the fall (reserves dropped $14.88 bn in one week, as reported), but it cannot hold the rupee at a fixed level.

rateCycle.title: RBI interest rate: cut in 2025, raised now
rateCycle.note: The RBI cut its rate four times in 2025, from 6.50% to 5.25%, held it there at four meetings, then raised it on 7 Oct 2026. The US raised its rate on 16 Sep 2026.

rupeeSides.title: A weak rupee (₹96): who loses, who gains
losers: Oil companies and India's import bill
Students and families paying fees abroad
Shoppers, as imported goods cost more
winners: IT and service exporters (TCS AI revenue: $3.1 bn)

quiz.q: Crude oil is not yet taxed under GST. What can raise GST on imports even if the amount imported stays the same?
options: A weaker rupee, because GST on imports is charged on their rupee value
quiz.why: GST on imports (IGST) is charged on the value of the goods in rupees. When a dollar costs about 8% more rupees, the same import carries more tax. This is one reason, not the whole story, behind import GST rising 25.9% in September 2026.

quiz.q: In July 2026, while the CJP protests were growing, what did foreign investors do in Indian shares?
quiz.why: They bought more than they sold. Protests move markets only when they might change policy, taxes or spending. The big selling of ₹35,861 crore came in September, after the US raised its rates.

quiz.q: After 7 October 2026, which RBI rate is the lowest in its band, the rate it pays banks that park money with it?
quiz.why: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF), at 5.25%, is the lowest rate: what the RBI pays banks that park money with it. The highest is the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate, at 5.75%.
